name: spires-arrival
note: CONTROL: the shipped arrival, exactly as the J menu resolves it. Pale-violet crystal blades, lamp-lit seabed, no rock needle.
setup: subwave.worldClock.setDayFraction(0.32); subwave.hud.visible=false; for (const id of ['controls','lock-hint','jump-toast','jump-menu','boot']) { const el=document.getElementById(id); if (el) el.style.display='none'; } subwave.jumpTo('spires'); const p0=subwave.player; const XX=p0.position[0], YY=p0.position[1], ZZ=p0.position[2], YW=p0.yaw, PT=p0.pitch; const p=subwave.player, c=subwave.renderer.camera; const X=XX, Y=YY, Z=ZZ, YAW=YW, PIT=PT; window.__pin=(window.__pin||0)+1; const tok=window.__pin; (function s(){ if(window.__pin!==tok) return; p.inVessel=false; p.position[0]=X; p.position[1]=Y; p.position[2]=Z; p.prevPosition.set(p.position); p.velocity.fill(0); p.oxygen=p.oxygenCapacity; p.health=100; p.yaw=YAW; p.pitch=PIT; c.setEuler(YAW,PIT,0); p.lampOn=Math.max(0,-p.position[1])>150; requestAnimationFrame(s); })();

name: spires-in-beam-32m
note: FAILURE 1, INSIDE THE BEAM. A ridge crest 42.7 m above the eye at 32 m, 34 m north-west of the resolved anchor,, i.e. inside PLAYER_LAMP.range (48 m). debugReadDepth(60) reads near-mass 0.244 and a minimum depth of 22.5 m at this pose, so a quarter of the frame IS the rock - and it delivers an amorphous glow with no edge. NOTE 2026-08-05: this pose is also 377 m deep and carries 1.04e-3 of surface daylight, so the in-beam explanation and the no-backdrop explanation are not separated by this frame alone.

name: spires-silhouette-60m
note: SUCCESS, AND NOT A ROCK SPIRES ARRIVAL - the note here previously blamed the landform-slope band and that was measured wrong on 2026-08-05. A 105 m-prominence tower 60 m away, crest 41.2 deg, just outside the 48 m beam: unlit rock against lit haze reads as a dark needle. What makes it read is the BACKDROP and not the range - this site is 292 m deep and carries 4.93e-3 of surface daylight, where every frame the same search took below 340 m carries 2.0e-3 or less and is empty. And the ground 12 m away at (1768, 1048) classifies as SHELF BREAK: the site is a Rock Spires / Shelf Break mosaic in which 4 of 169 cells on a 4 m lattice qualify at all. Relaxing the slope band admits this site and does not win it. See src/world/biome_anchors.js above LANDMARK_HEADINGS.

name: spires-past-band-81m
note: FAILURE 2, PAST THE BAND. An isolated crest 29.1 deg up at 81 m, 1.69 x the lamp range. The in-scatter behind it has faded to the rock own value and the frame is empty water. NOTE 2026-08-05: 407 m deep, 3.33e-5 of surface daylight. Read together with the 60 m success at 4.93e-3, the depth explains these frames and the distance does not.
